Connect a Meta ad account with a system user access token that grants ads_read. The token is asked
for without showing it, or piped in with --token-stdin; it is never passed as a flag's value.

Without an account, you choose from the accounts the token reads. The first sync starts right away
and reads --backfill-days of history.

Usage:
  voidhash ads connect [account] [flags]

Arguments:
  account  The Meta ad account id, with or without act_ (default: choose from the token's accounts)

Flags:
      --backfill-days <days>  History the first sync reads, in days (default: 90, at most 1095)
  -h, --help                  Show help for this command
      --json                  Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --project <project>     Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default:
                              this directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet                 Print only ids, one per line
      --token-stdin           Read the access token from standard input instead of asking for it

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash ads connect
  voidhash ads connect act_1234567890
  voidhash ads connect 1234567890 --token-stdin --backfill-days 365 < token.txt
